sections.title: Graphic Design and Image Production for Publishing

lead.text: A scholarly journal may need figures formatted according to its technical requirements. An educational book may contain diagrams, charts and illustrations that need consistent presentation. A digital publication may require images in different dimensions or file formats.

Some assets may have insufficient resolution, inconsistent labels, unsuitable proportions or missing editable elements. Others may need to be recreated from supplied references or adapted for different editions.
EPUBTRANS supports selected image and artwork production tasks according to the publisher's requirements, available source materials and agreed deliverables.
Our focus is on preparing visual content for publishing production, not replacing the publisher's editorial, scientific or design-approval responsibilities.

blocks.text: Books and journals often include figures that must follow defined presentation requirements.
Artwork preparation can involve reviewing supplied figures and adapting their presentation for the intended publication format.
Depending on the assignment, relevant work may include:

items: Preparing agreed outputs for typesetting or further review

blocks.text: The publisher should provide the relevant figure requirements, especially where artwork must fit a specified column width, publication template or digital output.
Scientific and technical content must remain faithful to the supplied source.
Some projects require existing artwork to be redrawn or converted into a more suitable editable form.
This may involve diagrams, line illustrations, explanatory graphics or other supplied visual references.
EPUBTRANS can assess eligible artwork recreation and illustration requirements based on the complexity of the source, the intended output and the available design tools.
It is important to distinguish between:

items: Adapting the appearance of supplied artwork
Creating a new illustration from an approved brief
Developing a new scientific or technical explanation

blocks.text: These activities have different requirements and should be quoted separately where appropriate.
New scientific interpretations, missing research data and technical conclusions must be supplied or approved by the responsible author, publisher or subject-matter specialist.
Publication images may require technical preparation before they can be incorporated into page layouts or digital outputs.
Depending on the source materials and approved requirements, relevant tasks may include:
Not every image can be improved sufficiently for every intended output.
For example, enlarging a low-resolution source or changing its resolution metadata cannot reliably recreate detail that is absent from the original.
Image processing must also respect applicable scientific image-integrity policies and should not misrepresent research results.
Charts and diagrams often need consistent styling, labels, typography and proportions across a publication.
EPUBTRANS can assess the preparation or adaptation of supplied visual information into an agreed publication design.
Projects may involve:

items: Preparing graphics for different publication sizes
Revising infographic layouts using approved content
Preparing editable visual assets where supported

blocks.text: Source data, figure values and scientific interpretations remain subject to author or publisher approval.
Creating statistical analyses, checking research findings or inventing missing data is outside routine graphic production.

groups.title: Graphics for Books and Educational Publications

blocks.text: Illustrated books, textbooks, manuals and other educational publications may include a combination of diagrams, figures, callouts, icons and photographs.
Artwork may need to remain consistent across chapters or editions.
Depending on the agreed scope, production support can involve preparing visual assets, adapting supplied illustrations and coordinating image requirements with the typesetting process.
Book cover concepts and full cover production are addressed separately through EPUBTRANS's Cover Page Design Services.

groups.title: Graphics for Localization and Multilingual Content

blocks.text: Localized publications may contain illustrations or images with embedded text.
After the approved translation is available, some graphics may need editing to accommodate longer text, different scripts or revised labels.
EPUBTRANS can assess graphics adaptation as part of a broader localization production requirement.
The feasibility depends on access to editable source artwork, approved translated content, appropriate fonts and compatible tools.
Linguistic translation and language review are distinct from graphics editing unless separately commissioned.

sections.title: Artwork Preparation for Books and Scholarly Journals

lead.text: Different publication types require different visual-production approaches.

blocks.text: Journal figures may be governed by detailed requirements for dimensions, resolution, format, typography, labeling and panel organization.
Some journals also have strict policies governing image manipulation, especially for photographs, microscopy, medical images and other scientific evidence.
The target journal's instructions and approved source artwork should be provided before production begins.
EPUBTRANS can assess the applicable artwork-formatting requirements but cannot guarantee journal acceptance solely because an image has been formatted.
Book production may involve chapter illustrations, diagrams, figures, photographic images and recurring visual elements.
The supplied page design, trim size and intended print or digital output can influence artwork preparation.
When an image is intended for typesetting, its final dimensions and relationship to surrounding content should be coordinated with the production specification.
Professional manuals, reports and training materials may contain explanatory graphics, charts, tables and visual instructions.
These can be assessed for visual consistency, source-file preparation and delivery in the required format.
Educational accuracy and subject-matter interpretation remain separate responsibilities.

sections.title: Image Quality, Technical Requirements and Research Integrity

lead.text: Artwork quality should be evaluated against the actual source materials and publication specifications.

blocks.text: Images intended for print or digital publication may have different dimension and resolution requirements.
The project should identify the intended output size and any specific requirements supplied by the publisher, printer or platform.
A low-resolution image may require a better original or separate recreation rather than simple enlargement.
The most appropriate output depends on the artwork type and intended use.
Publishing projects may involve raster images, vector artwork, PDFs or native design files.
The ability to return an editable file depends on the source, available assets, software compatibility and commissioned production work.
Some projects require specific color spaces, fonts, line widths or image treatment.
The supplied specifications should guide these decisions, rather than assuming that one color or image setting is suitable for all print and digital environments.
For scientific and medical publications, image adjustments must not introduce, remove, conceal or misleadingly emphasize research information.
Cropping, contrast adjustments, retouching and other image changes may be restricted by the journal's image-integrity policy.

The publisher or author should provide approved originals and instructions. Any required disclosures, scientific review or evidence verification remain with the responsible parties unless a separate service is agreed.
EPUBTRANS's routine graphics production should not be interpreted as a research-integrity investigation or certification.
A clearly prepared visual is not automatically accessible to every reader.
Alternative text, accessible document structure, color-contrast evaluation and other accessibility work may require separate specifications and testing.
Please refer to our Accessibility Services for supported accessibility-related production requirements.

lead.text: Complete artwork and clear specifications help identify the right production approach.

blocks.text: Useful inputs may include:

items: Captions, labels and other approved text
Relevant source data for charts, where applicable
Localization text, if graphics require language adaptation

blocks.text: For scholarly images, unmodified original files and the target journal's image policies may also be necessary.
Editable vector files offer different options from flattened images or screenshots.
A project involving straightforward resizing may require relatively little intervention, while recreation from poor-quality references may involve substantial manual work.
We assess these differences before defining the scope.

lead.text: The final outputs depend on the commissioned work and the intended publishing workflow.

items: Images exported to agreed dimensions and formats
Editable design assets, where available and included
Artwork prepared for integration into page-layout files
Issue lists or review notes, where commissioned

lead.text: File formats must be confirmed for each project.
Examples of publishing image formats include TIFF, JPEG, PNG, EPS, SVG and PDF, but support for a particular version, feature or native application file must be verified before production.
The delivery agreement should specify the required formats, editable-file expectations, number of versions and correction responsibilities.

sections.title: Our Graphic Design and Image Production Workflow

blocks.text: We review the supplied images, reference files, publication requirements and intended outputs.
Missing editable files, unclear labels and technical concerns can be identified at this stage.
We clarify which artwork activities are required and which remain the responsibility of the publisher, designer or author.
This includes output formats, permitted adjustments, review stages and any required source-preservation rules.

groups.title: 3. Prepare or Adapt the Visual Assets

blocks.text: The agreed artwork preparation, editing, illustration adaptation or related tasks are performed using an appropriate supported workflow.
Changes requiring editorial or scientific decisions are referred to the responsible reviewer.
Depending on the project, visual and technical checks may cover dimensions, labels, file integrity, formatting and consistency with the supplied specification.
A proof or sample may be provided for review when included in the agreement.
Approved files are organized according to the delivery requirements.
Any separately commissioned source files, asset packages or outstanding notes are included as agreed.

lead.text: The quality review depends on the type of artwork, publication requirements and commissioned activities.

blocks.text: Checks may address alignment, spacing, font appearance, labeling and consistency across a related set of assets.
Where included, checks can address file dimensions, format, resolution information and basic file integrity.
Recreated or adapted artwork may require comparison against the supplied source or approved reference.
This review must distinguish presentation changes from changes to content meaning.
The publisher or its designated reviewer remains responsible for confirming editorial accuracy, scientific meaning, rights clearance and acceptance of the final artwork.
The agreed QA process does not automatically establish scientific validity, copyright clearance, accessibility conformance or third-party platform acceptance.

sections.title: What Affects Project Scope and Scheduling?

blocks.text: Low-quality scans, incomplete diagrams and missing editable files can require additional preparation.
A small collection of simple figures differs from a larger project containing detailed diagrams, illustrations and multilayer artwork.
Resizing an existing image, redrawing a supplied figure and designing an original illustration are different tasks.
Print and digital outputs may need different dimensions, image characteristics and file formats.
Missing permissions, incomplete scientific source information or unapproved figure changes can affect the project.
Additional design options, revision rounds, delayed publisher feedback or changes to approved source content can affect the agreed scope.
These factors are reviewed before project estimates and delivery arrangements are confirmed.
Cover design for suitable books, journals and other publication requirements.
Page composition and the integration of approved figures and other visual assets into book and journal layouts.
A broader overview of editorial, print and digital production services for publishers.
Document layout, editable content preparation and multilingual desktop publishing workflows.
PDF reconstruction, OCR and related document conversion when source materials need additional preparation.
EPUB creation and digital publication production using suitable content and visual assets.
Accessibility-related production and remediation for supported publication and document formats.

groups.title: What does EPUBTRANS's Graphic Design & Image Services offering include?

blocks.text: The documented service portfolio covers graphic design and production-related image work. The existing offering includes illustrations, infographics, charts, image preparation and editing. The exact tasks and outputs are confirmed for each assignment.

groups.title: Can EPUBTRANS prepare figures for academic journals?

blocks.text: Journal figure preparation can be assessed against supplied artwork, journal instructions and technical specifications. Any format-specific or scientific-image requirements must be confirmed before production.

groups.title: Do you provide figure redrawing services?

blocks.text: Eligible figure redrawing and artwork recreation can be assessed. The feasibility depends on the available source, content complexity, required editability and approved reference material.

groups.title: Can you improve a low-resolution image?

blocks.text: Some image preparation may be possible, but enlarging a low-resolution file cannot reliably recover detail missing from the original. A higher-quality source or approved artwork recreation may be necessary.

groups.title: Can you create charts and infographics?

blocks.text: Graphic preparation and infographic-related work appear in the existing service offering. Requirements for new designs, data visualization, research interpretation and editable outputs need separate scope confirmation.

groups.title: Do you support image editing for scientific publications?

blocks.text: Suitable technical preparation can be assessed, but changes must comply with the target publication's image-integrity requirements. Scientific data must not be misleadingly altered.

groups.title: Can you provide editable artwork files?

blocks.text: Editable deliverables depend on the source material, design application and agreed work. Please identify the required native file format when requesting a quote.

groups.title: Do you work with Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator files?

blocks.text: EPUBTRANS has historically documented experience with Photoshop and Illustrator-related production assets. Current application versions, supported features and export requirements must be confirmed before the project.

groups.title: Can you adapt images containing translated text?

blocks.text: Graphics requiring post-translation text integration can be assessed where approved translations, suitable fonts and editable artwork are available. Linguistic review is separately scoped.

groups.title: Are book cover design services included?

blocks.text: Book and journal cover design requirements are covered by a separate EPUBTRANS service. Please review our Cover Page Design Services page for that scope.
Not automatically. Alternative text and accessibility remediation have separate requirements that should be agreed with the applicable Accessibility Services scope.

groups.title: What information is needed for an artwork quotation?

blocks.text: Please provide representative artwork, the number of assets, intended publication, current file formats, output specifications, available editable sources, required changes and preferred schedule.
